summary: Romania joined the Schengen Area on 1 January 2025: EU citizens travel with a passport or national ID card, visa-exempt nationalities such as the US and UK get 90 days in any 180-day period counted together with the rest of the Schengen Area, and other passports need a Schengen visa applied for via Romania's official eVisa portal. The currency is the leu.

tips.text: Romania's currency is the leu (RON), not the euro. Canada's travel advice says exchanging money on the street is illegal: change euros at recognized exchange shops, banks or hotels.
Romania joined the Schengen Area on 1 January 2025, so days spent in Romania count toward the same 90-in-180 allowance as the other Schengen countries.

Before hiking or other activities in the Carpathians, Canada's travel advice says to check the Salvamont mountain rescue service for current risks. In an emergency, including wild animal encounters, the Romanian government sends RO-ALERT text messages to all active SIM cards.

Canada's travel advice says to use only licensed metered taxis that display their price lists, not to hail a taxi on the street but to order one from your hotel or use a trusted ride-sharing app, and at Bucharest's Henri Coandă airport to take a taxi from the booth in the arrivals terminal to get a fair rate.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Romania?
faq.answer: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens don't need a visa. Citizens of the Schengen visa-waiver countries — including the US, UK, Canada, Australia and Japan — can stay 90 days in any 180-day period without a visa. Other nationalities need a Schengen short-stay visa, applied for through Romania's official eVisa portal (evisa.mae.ro) and the consulate serving their residence.

faq.question: Is Romania in the Schengen Area?
faq.answer: Yes. The European Commission says Bulgaria and Romania were the last countries to join the Schengen Area, on 1 January 2025.

faq.question: Does Romania use the euro?
faq.answer: No. The currency is the Romanian leu (RON). Canada's travel advice says credit cards are widely accepted in major urban centres although the economy is primarily cash-based, and that euros should be exchanged at recognized exchange shops, banks or hotels; exchanging money on the street is illegal.

faq.question: Do days in Romania count toward the Schengen 90/180 limit?
faq.answer: Yes. Romania has been in the Schengen Area since 1 January 2025, and the 90 days in any 180-day period are counted across the whole Schengen Area rather than per country.

faq.question: Can Moldovan citizens travel to Romania visa-free?
faq.answer: Yes — Moldovan citizens with a biometric passport can enter visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period under the EU's visa-free regime.
